- Trust decision: the decoder decides whether an attacker-supplied PFX is authentic by recomputing the MAC from the file's own PBKDF2 parameters; the fix makes it reject PBMAC1 keyLength < 20 (`mac.go:123-131`, reached by `Decode`/`DecodeChain`/`DecodeTrustStore`/`ToPEM` through `pkcs12.go:573`).
- `pattern_fit`: `injection_only` — no real O2 site or O8 route; all four entry points funnel into one `doPBMAC1` check, so sibling room exists only if planted (`crypto.go:207-260`, `mac.go:42-61`).
- Strongest lever: `O5` — no-MacData acceptance with an empty password (`pkcs12.go:569-572`) is legitimate and documented, so an over-broad "MAC always required" fix breaks passwordless decoding.
- Biggest red flag: `single_site` (plus `tiny_repo`): a four-line guard in one function of a 17-file library, roughly 15 minutes of work.
- Unverified: measured repo MB, whether any RFC 9579 test vector uses keyLength < 20, and the `j_multi_site` rule-vs-reality mismatch noted in the file.
